\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The problem}

Let $\Omega$ be a finite set and let $A_1,\dots,A_k$ be subsets of $\Omega$. The
\emph{first marginals} of this family are the numbers $|A_i|$; the \emph{second
marginals} are the numbers $|A_i\cap A_j|$. More generally, for a subfamily
$T\subseteq\{1,\dots,k\}$ the \emph{joint marginal of order $|T|$} is
$\bigl|\bigcap_{i\in T}A_i\bigr|$.

The quantity one usually wants is the size of the union
$\bigl|\bigcup_i A_i\bigr|$. Inclusion--exclusion expresses it in terms of
\emph{all} marginals, but the alternating sum has $2^k-1$ terms and requires
data of every order. Truncating after the first order gives the union bound
$\sum_i|A_i|\ge|U|$; after the second order it gives the classical Bonferroni
inequality $\sum_i|A_i|-\sum_{i<j}|A_i\cap A_j|\le|U|$.

Two questions organise this paper.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{How lossy are these truncations, exactly?} Not in the worst case,
but \emph{exactly}: is there a closed form for the defect, and which families
make it vanish?
\item \textbf{Is the truncation to low order an artefact of the method, or a
genuine information barrier?} Could some non-linear function of the low-order
marginals compute the union?
\end{enumerate}

Question 1 has a complete answer: every Bonferroni-type inequality in this
family is an \emph{identity minus an explicit nonnegative functional}, each
functional being a moment of a single scalar function. Question 2 has a complete
answer too, negative in the strongest possible sense: for every $k$ there is a
proper obstruction at every order below $k$.

\subsection{Motivation from ensemble learning}

Fix a finite sample space $\Omega$ of size $N$ and a finite collection of
hypotheses indexed by $I$. Let $A_i$ be the set of samples on which hypothesis
$i$ fails. Then $|A_i|$ is the empirical error count of hypothesis $i$;
$|A_i\cap A_j|$ is the empirical co-failure count of the pair $(i,j)$---the raw
ingredient of every pairwise diversity metric used in ensemble design;
$U=\bigcup_i A_i$ is the set of samples on which the ensemble is not unanimously
correct; $d(x)$ is the number of members failing at sample $x$; and
$D=\{x: d(x)\ge 2\}$ is the set of samples where failures are \emph{correlated}.
Theorem~\ref{thm:threshold} below constructs, for every $k$, two ensembles
indistinguishable by every marginal of order $<k$ whose total error supports
differ---a hard limit on the expressive power of low-order diversity metrics.

\section{The multiplicity calculus}

Throughout, $\Omega$ is a set with decidable equality, $I$ is a finite index set
of size $k=|I|$, and $A: I\to\PP_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Omega)$ is a family of finite
subsets of $\Omega$.

\begin{definition}[Multiplicity]
The \emph{coverage multiplicity} of $x\in\Omega$ is
$d(x)=\#\{i\in I: x\in A_i\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Cover]
The \emph{cover} of the family is $U=\bigcup_{i\in I}A_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Double-collision set]
The \emph{double-collision set} is $D=\{x\in U: d(x)\ge 2\}$.
\end{definition}

Immediately, $x\in U$ iff $d(x)>0$; hence $d(x)\ge 1$ on $U$, a fact used
repeatedly below. Also $A_i\subseteq U$ for each $i\in I$.

\begin{lemma}[Indicator expansion]\label{lem:ind}
For every $x\in\Omega$, $\;d(x)=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf 1[x\in A_i]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The cardinality of a filtered finite set is the sum of the indicator of its
predicate.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[First moment identity]\label{thm:m1}
Let $S$ be a finite set with $A_i\subseteq S$ for all $i\in I$. Then
$\sum_{x\in S}d(x)=\sum_{i\in I}|A_i|$. In particular
$\sum_{x\in U}d(x)=\sum_{i\in I}|A_i|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Expand $d$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:ind} and exchange summation:
$\sum_{x\in S}\sum_{i}\mathbf 1[x\in A_i]=\sum_i|A_i\cap S|=\sum_i|A_i|$, using
$A_i\subseteq S$. This is Fubini for the incidence relation
$\{(x,i):x\in A_i\}$: counting incidences by point, then by set.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Second moment identity]\label{thm:m2}
Under the same hypotheses,
$\sum_{x\in S}d(x)^2=\sum_{(i,j)\in I\times I}|A_i\cap A_j|$, the sum running
over \emph{ordered} pairs, diagonal included.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Squaring Lemma~\ref{lem:ind} and expanding the product of two sums gives the
pointwise identity
$d(x)^2=\sum_{(i,j)}\mathbf 1[x\in A_i]\mathbf 1[x\in A_j]
=\sum_{(i,j)}\mathbf 1[x\in A_i\cap A_j]$, verified by the four cases of
$(x\in A_i?, x\in A_j?)$. Exchanging summation and using
$A_i\cap A_j\subseteq S$ gives the claim. This is Fubini for the triple
incidence relation $\{(x,i,j): x\in A_i\cap A_j\}$.
\end{proof}

Theorems~\ref{thm:m1} and \ref{thm:m2} say that \emph{the first- and
second-order marginal data of a family is exactly the pair of first two moments
of one scalar function on the cover.} Whatever those two moments cannot see, the
marginals cannot see either---a heuristic made precise in
Section~\ref{sec:threshold}.

\begin{lemma}[Diagonal splitting]\label{lem:diag}
$\sum_{(i,j)\in I\times I}|A_i\cap A_j|=\sum_{i\in I}|A_i|+\sum_{i\neq j}|A_i\cap A_j|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{corollary}[Off-diagonal mass as a factorial moment]\label{cor:offdiag}
$\displaystyle \Sig_2:=\sum_{i\neq j}|A_i\cap A_j|=\sum_{x\in U}d(x)\bigl(d(x)-1\bigr)$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Combine Theorems~\ref{thm:m1}, \ref{thm:m2} and Lemma~\ref{lem:diag} with the
pointwise identity $d^2=d(d-1)+d$, valid without truncation issues since
$d(x)\ge 1$ on $U$.
\end{proof}

The quantity $d(x)(d(x)-1)$ counts ordered pairs of distinct members containing
$x$, so $\Sig_2$ counts ordered collisions. We write
\[
\Sig_1:=\sum_{i\in I}|A_i|,\qquad \Sig_2:=\sum_{i\neq j}|A_i\cap A_j|,\qquad
\Stot:=\sum_{i,j}|A_i\cap A_j|=\Sig_1+\Sig_2 .
\]

\section{The Bonferroni defect identity}

\begin{theorem}[Bonferroni defect identity]\label{thm:defect}
For every finite family,
\[
\Sig_1+\sum_{x\in U}\bigl(d(x)-1\bigr)^2 \;=\; |U|+\Sig_2 .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Corollary~\ref{cor:offdiag} and Theorem~\ref{thm:m1}, the right-hand side is
$\sum_{x\in U}\bigl(1+d(x)(d(x)-1)\bigr)$ and the left-hand side is
$\sum_{x\in U}\bigl(d(x)+(d(x)-1)^2\bigr)$; the summands agree pointwise since
$1+d^2-d=d+d^2-2d+1$. Over the natural numbers one writes $d(x)=1+c$ with
$c\ge 0$, valid on the cover, so the subtraction is genuine.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Irregularity functional]
The \emph{Bonferroni defect}, or \emph{irregularity}, is
$\Irr(I,A)=\sum_{x\in U}(d(x)-1)^2\ge 0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Second Bonferroni inequality, off-diagonal form]\label{cor:bonf}
$\displaystyle \sum_{i\in I}|A_i|\;\le\;\Bigl|\bigcup_{i\in I}A_i\Bigr|+\sum_{i\neq j}|A_i\cap A_j|$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Drop the nonnegative defect in Theorem~\ref{thm:defect}. In inequality form the
argument is the pointwise bound $2d\le 1+d^2$---the square completion
$(d-1)^2\ge 0$---summed over $U$.
\end{proof}

\section{The sharp Bonferroni inequality and the double-collision bound}

The classical second Bonferroni inequality sums over unordered pairs and is a
factor $2$ stronger on the correction. Written index-order-free, it reads
$2\Sig_1\le 2|U|+\Sig_2$, and it too has an exact defect---of a different, more
informative shape.

\begin{theorem}[Sharp Bonferroni defect identity]\label{thm:sharpdefect}
\[
2\,\Sig_1+\sum_{x\in U}\bigl(d(x)-1\bigr)\bigl(d(x)-2\bigr)\;=\;2\,|U|+\Sig_2 .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Reduce to a pointwise identity on the cover. Writing $d=1+c$ with $c\ge 0$, the
claim is $2(1+c)+c(c-1)=2+(1+c)c$. The case $c=0$ is checked separately, the
defect term vanishing there since $d-1=0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sharp second Bonferroni inequality]\label{cor:sharp}
$\displaystyle 2\sum_i|A_i|\le 2\Bigl|\bigcup_i A_i\Bigr|+\sum_{i\neq j}|A_i\cap A_j|$,
equivalently $\displaystyle \sum_i|A_i|-\sum_{i<j}|A_i\cap A_j|\le\Bigl|\bigcup_i A_i\Bigr|$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
$(d-1)(d-2)\ge 0$ for every integer $d\ge 0$: it is zero at $d\in\{1,2\}$ and
positive for $d\ge 3$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}
Corollary~\ref{cor:sharp} implies Corollary~\ref{cor:bonf}: from
$2\Sig_1\le 2|U|+\Sig_2$ and $\Sig_2\ge 0$ one gets $2\Sig_1\le 2(|U|+\Sig_2)$.
\end{proposition}

The change of defect from $(d-1)^2$ to $(d-1)(d-2)$ is the content of this
section. The first vanishes only at $d=1$; the second vanishes on all of
$\{1,2\}$. The extremal class widens from ``pairwise disjoint'' to ``no point
covered three times''---and that class is shared with a second inequality.

\begin{theorem}[Double-collision bound]\label{thm:dc}
$\displaystyle 2\,|D|\;\le\;\sum_{i\neq j}|A_i\cap A_j|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Corollary~\ref{cor:offdiag} the right side is $\sum_{x\in U}d(x)(d(x)-1)$.
Restrict to $D$ (legitimate, all summands nonnegative); on $D$ we have $d\ge 2$
and $d-1\ge 1$, hence $d(d-1)\ge 2$. Summing the constant $2$ over $D$ gives
$2|D|$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Ensemble reading]
If every pair among $k$ hypotheses co-fails on at most $t$ samples, then at most
$k(k-1)t/2$ samples see two or more simultaneous failures.
\end{corollary}

A covered point that is not a double collision lies in exactly one member, since
$1\le d(x)<2$ forces $d(x)=1$.

\section{The Cauchy--Schwarz upgrade}

The Bonferroni route compares $d$ pointwise to the constant $1$; when the family
is far from a partition this is wasteful. Comparing $d$ to its own mean instead
yields an incomparably better bound in that regime.

\begin{lemma}[Lagrange identity]\label{lem:lagrange}
For any finite $S$ and any $f: S\to\mathbb Z$,
\[
2\Bigl(|S|\sum_{x\in S}f(x)^2-\Bigl(\sum_{x\in S}f(x)\Bigr)^{\!2}\Bigr)
=\sum_{x\in S}\sum_{y\in S}\bigl(f(x)-f(y)\bigr)^2 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Expand $(f(x)-f(y))^2$ and sum over $y$ first: the inner sum is
$|S|f(x)^2-2f(x)\sum_y f(y)+\sum_y f(y)^2$. Summing over $x$ gives
$2|S|\sum f^2-2(\sum f)^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Second-moment / Cauchy--Schwarz bound]\label{thm:cs}
$\displaystyle \Bigl(\sum_{i\in I}|A_i|\Bigr)^{\!2}\;\le\;\Bigl|\bigcup_i A_i\Bigr|\cdot\sum_{(i,j)\in I\times I}|A_i\cap A_j|$,
i.e.\ $\Sig_1^2\le|U|\cdot\Stot$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:lagrange} with $S=U$ and $f=d$ over $\mathbb Z$. The right
side is a sum of squares, hence nonnegative, so $(\sum_U d)^2\le|U|\sum_U d^2$;
substitute Theorems~\ref{thm:m1} and \ref{thm:m2}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Cauchy--Schwarz gap]\label{def:gap}
The \emph{gap} of a family is the integer
\[
g=|U|\cdot\sum_{x\in U}d(x)^2-\Bigl(\sum_{x\in U}d(x)\Bigr)^{\!2}
 =|U|\cdot\Stot-\Sig_1^2\;\ge\;0 .
\]
\end{definition}

The two expressions agree by Theorems~\ref{thm:m1}--\ref{thm:m2}; the second
shows $g$ is computable from the marginals alone, and the first shows
$g=\tfrac12\sum_{x,y\in U}(d(x)-d(y))^2$. This double description is what makes
the stability theory work: a statistic one can measure controls a structural
quantity one cannot.

\section{Rigidity: exactly which families are extremal}

\begin{definition}[Regular cover]
The family is a \emph{$d_0$-regular cover} if $d(x)=d_0$ for all $x\in U$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}
If the family is a $d_0$-regular cover then $\sum_i|A_i|=d_0\,|U|$.
\end{proposition}

Each rigidity theorem below is read off the corresponding defect identity: an
inequality obtained by discarding a nonnegative defect is an equality exactly
when the defect---a sum of nonnegative terms---vanishes termwise.

\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the second Bonferroni inequality]\label{thm:rig1}
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\sum_i|A_i|=|U|+\sum_{i\neq j}|A_i\cap A_j|$;
\item $d(x)=1$ for every $x\in U$;
\item the family is pairwise disjoint: $A_i\cap A_j=\emptyset$ for $i\neq j$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(1)$\Leftrightarrow$(2): by Theorem~\ref{thm:defect}, (1) holds iff
$\Irr=\sum_{x\in U}(d(x)-1)^2=0$, iff every summand vanishes. (2)$\Rightarrow$(3):
a point of $A_i\cap A_j$ with $i\neq j$ is covered with $d\ge 2$.
(3)$\Rightarrow$(2): a covered point in two distinct members contradicts
disjointness.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the double-collision bound]\label{thm:rig2}
Equality $2|D|=\sum_{i\neq j}|A_i\cap A_j|$ holds iff $d(x)\le 2$ for all
$x\in U$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Write the right side as $\sum_{x\in U}d(x)(d(x)-1)$ and split over $D$ and
$U\setminus D$. On $U\setminus D$ we have $d=1$ and those terms vanish; on $D$,
$d(d-1)$ equals $2$ iff $d=2$ and exceeds $2$ iff $d\ge 3$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the sharp Bonferroni inequality]\label{thm:rig3}
Equality $2\Sig_1=2|U|+\Sig_2$ holds iff $d(x)\le 2$ for all $x\in U$. Hence the
sharp Bonferroni inequality and the double-collision bound have the same
extremal class, and each is tight exactly when the other is.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Theorem~\ref{thm:sharpdefect}, equality holds iff
$\sum_{x\in U}(d(x)-1)(d(x)-2)=0$; each summand is a nonnegative integer
vanishing exactly when $d(x)\in\{1,2\}$, and $d\ge 1$ on $U$. Combine with
Theorem~\ref{thm:rig2}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the second-moment bound]\label{thm:rig4}
Equality $\Sig_1^2=|U|\cdot\Stot$ holds iff the family is a regular cover.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:lagrange} and Definition~\ref{def:gap},
$2g=\sum_{x,y\in U}(d(x)-d(y))^2$. Equality means $g=0$, hence every squared
difference vanishes, hence $d$ is constant on $U$ (the empty cover being
trivial). The converse is immediate.
\end{proof}

The three theorems delineate a hierarchy of extremal classes:
$\{\text{pairwise disjoint}\}\subsetneq\{d\le 2\}$ and
$\{\text{pairwise disjoint}\}\subsetneq\{\text{regular}\}$, with $\{d\le 2\}$
and $\{\text{regular}\}$ incomparable. Choosing which bound to apply to a family
is exactly the question of which extremal class it is nearest.

\section{Stability: near-tightness forces near-regularity}

\begin{theorem}[Spread bound]\label{thm:spread}
For any two covered points $x,y\in U$, $\;\bigl(d(x)-d(y)\bigr)^2\le g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:lagrange}, $2g=\sum_{u,v\in U}(d(u)-d(v))^2$. The double sum
contains the terms indexed by $(x,y)$ and $(y,x)$, each equal to
$(d(x)-d(y))^2$; all other terms are nonnegative.
\end{proof}

Thus the entire spread $\max_U d-\min_U d$ is at most $\sqrt g$. Since $g$ is
computable from the marginals, this is a usable statement: a measured
second-order profile close to extremal certifies a structural conclusion about
the unmeasured multiplicity profile.

\begin{corollary}
If $g=0$ then the family is a regular cover.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Integrality gives a hard threshold]\label{cor:hard}
If $g<1$ then $d$ is constant on $U$. Equivalently, either the family is exactly
regular or $g\ge 1$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[The Bonferroni defect is controlled by the gap]\label{thm:defgap}
Suppose the family has average multiplicity $1$ on its cover, i.e.\
$\sum_{x\in U}d(x)=|U|$ (equivalently $\Sig_1=|U|$). Then
$\;|U|\cdot\Irr(I,A)=g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$\sum_U(d-1)^2=\sum_U d^2-2\sum_U d+|U|=\sum_U d^2-|U|$ under the hypothesis.
Multiplying by $|U|$ gives $|U|\sum_U d^2-(\sum_U d)^2=g$.
\end{proof}

So under the natural normalisation the Bonferroni defect and the Cauchy--Schwarz
gap are the same quantity up to the factor $|U|$: the two families of
inequalities are quantitatively linked, not merely analogous.

\section{The marginal-order threshold}\label{sec:threshold}

\subsection{Second-order data is insufficient}

\begin{definition}[The two witnesses]\label{def:witness}
On $\Omega=\{0,1,2,3\}$ define
\[
\textbf{Triangle: } A_0=\{0,1\},\;A_1=\{1,2\},\;A_2=\{2,0\};
\]
\[
\textbf{Sunflower: } B_0=\{0,1\},\;B_1=\{0,2\},\;B_2=\{0,3\}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:witness}
For all $i$, $|A_i|=|B_i|=2$; for all $i\neq j$,
$|A_i\cap A_j|=|B_i\cap B_j|=1$. Yet $\bigl|\bigcup_i A_i\bigr|=3$ and
$\bigl|\bigcup_i B_i\bigr|=4$. The third-order marginals differ:
$|A_0\cap A_1\cap A_2|=0$ while $|B_0\cap B_1\cap B_2|=1$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[No second-order formula]\label{thm:nof}
There is no function $F$ of the first- and second-order marginals with
$\bigl|\bigcup_i A_i\bigr|=F\bigl((|A_i|)_i,(|A_i\cap A_j|)_{i,j}\bigr)$ for all
families of three subsets of a four-element set. Consequently every statement
relating the union to first- and second-order marginals must be an inequality.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Such an $F$ would give $3=4$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:witness}.
\end{proof}

The witness pair also calibrates Sections 5--6 sharply. The triangle has
multiplicity profile $(2,2,2,0)$: a $2$-regular cover, gap
$g=3\cdot 12-6^2=0$, attaining Corr\'adi's bound with equality
($3\cdot 2^2=12=3\cdot(2+2\cdot 1)$). The sunflower has profile $(3,1,1,1)$: gap
$g=4\cdot 12-6^2=12>0$, Corr\'adi strict ($12<16$), and double-collision slack
($2|D|=2<6=\Sig_2$)---exactly as Theorem~\ref{thm:rig2} predicts, since it has a
point of multiplicity $3$.

\subsection{The positive direction: all orders suffice}

\begin{theorem}[Complete marginal data determines the union]\label{thm:incexc}
Let $A,B: I\to\PP_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Omega)$. If
$\bigl|\bigcap_{i\in T}A_i\bigr|=\bigl|\bigcap_{i\in T}B_i\bigr|$ for every
nonempty $T\subseteq I$, then
$\bigl|\bigcup_{i\in I}A_i\bigr|=\bigl|\bigcup_{i\in I}B_i\bigr|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Inclusion--exclusion:
$\bigl|\bigcup_{i\in I}A_i\bigr|=\sum_{\emptyset\neq T\subseteq I}(-1)^{|T|+1}\bigl|\bigcap_{i\in T}A_i\bigr|$
depends only on the hypothesised data.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Every order below $k$ is insufficient}

\begin{definition}[Joint marginals]
For $T\subseteq I$ write $J_A(T)=\bigcap_{i\in T}A_i$, with
$J_A(\emptyset)=\Omega$. The number $|J_A(T)|$ is the joint marginal of order
$|T|$.
\end{definition}

\paragraph{The construction.} Fix $k\ge 1$ and set
$\Omega_k=\PP(\{1,\dots,k\})\times\{\texttt{first},\texttt{second}\}$, of size
$2^{k+1}$: two labelled copies of every subset of the index set. Define, for
$i\in\{1,\dots,k\}$,
\[
\Plain_i=\bigl\{(S,\texttt{first}): i\in S\bigr\},\qquad
\Par_i=\bigl\{(S,b): i\in S,\ |S|\equiv k \bmod 2\bigr\}.
\]
Assign to each subset $S$ the weight $w(S)$ equal to the number of ground points
lying over $S$; then $w_{\Plain}(S)=1$ and $w_{\Par}(S)=1+(-1)^{k-|S|}$, so the
families differ by the perturbation $\delta(S)=(-1)^{k-|S|}$. For $T\neq\emptyset$
the joint marginal is the \emph{upper sum} $|J(T)|=\sum_{S\supseteq T}w(S)$,
since a point over $S$ lies in $\bigcap_{i\in T}$ exactly when $T\subseteq S$.

\begin{lemma}[The perturbation is invisible below the top]\label{lem:mobius}
For every $T\subsetneq\{1,\dots,k\}$, $\;\sum_{S\supseteq T}\delta(S)=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Supersets of $T$ correspond to subsets $U$ of $T^c$ via $S=T\cup U$, with
$|S|=|T|+|U|$. With $n=|T^c|=k-|T|\ge 1$,
$\sum_{S\supseteq T}\delta(S)=\pm\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^j\binom nj=0$ by the
alternating binomial identity. Concretely: exactly $2^{n-1}$ of the $2^n$
supersets of $T$ have size of each parity.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Marginals of order $<k$ never determine the union]\label{thm:threshold}
For every $k\ge 1$ the families $\Plain$ and $\Par$ on $\Omega_k$ satisfy:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $|J_{\Plain}(T)|=|J_{\Par}(T)|$ for every proper $T\subsetneq\{1,\dots,k\}$;
\item $|J_{\Plain}(\{1,\dots,k\})|=1\neq 2=|J_{\Par}(\{1,\dots,k\})|$;
\item $\bigl|\bigcup_i\Plain_i\bigr|\neq\bigl|\bigcup_i\Par_i\bigr|$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently no functional of the joint marginals of order $<k$ computes the
union of $k$ sets. With Theorem~\ref{thm:incexc}, the marginal-order threshold
for $k$ sets is exactly $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(1) For nonempty proper $T$: $|J_{\Plain}(T)|=2^{k-|T|}$ (all supersets, one copy
each) and $|J_{\Par}(T)|=2\cdot 2^{k-|T|-1}=2^{k-|T|}$ (half the supersets, two
copies each) by Lemma~\ref{lem:mobius}; for $T=\emptyset$ both equal
$|\Omega_k|$. (2) At the top the only superset is $\{1,\dots,k\}$, which has the
right parity. (3) $\Plain$ covers $\{(S,\texttt{first}): S\neq\emptyset\}$, of
size $2^k-1$, odd; $\Par$ covers a set of the form
$X\times\{\texttt{first},\texttt{second}\}$, of even size.
\end{proof}

The mechanism is representation-theoretic in flavour: $\delta(S)=(-1)^{k-|S|}$ is
the \emph{top M\"obius eigenvector} of the Boolean lattice---the unique function,
up to scale, all of whose upper sums vanish except at the top. It is exactly the
signal that low-order marginals are blind to.

\begin{corollary}[Ensemble reading]
For every $k$ there are two ensembles of $k$ hypotheses with identical
individual error rates, identical pairwise co-failure rates, and identical
$j$-wise co-failure rates for every $j<k$, whose total error supports differ in
size.
\end{corollary}

\section{Design-theoretic marginals: Corr\'adi and Fisher}

\begin{theorem}[Corr\'adi's inequality, division-free]\label{thm:corradi}
Let $|I|=k$, and suppose $|A_i|\ge m$ for all $i$ and $|A_i\cap A_j|\le t$ for
all $i\neq j$. Then
\[
k\,m^2\;\le\;\Bigl|\bigcup_{i\in I}A_i\Bigr|\cdot\bigl(m+(k-1)t\bigr),
\qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad
\Bigl|\bigcup_{i\in I}A_i\Bigr|\;\ge\;\frac{k\,m^2}{m+(k-1)t}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Set $N=|U|$ and $\Sig_1\ge km$. Theorem~\ref{thm:cs} gives
$\Sig_1^2\le N(\Sig_1+\Sig_2)$, and $\Sig_2\le k(k-1)t$. Hence with
$c=k(k-1)t$, $\Sig_1^2\le N(\Sig_1+c)$. The map $S\mapsto S^2/(S+c)$ is
nondecreasing, so $u^2\le N(u+c)$ for any $u\le\Sig_1$; taking $u=km$ yields
$k^2m^2\le kN(m+(k-1)t)$. The monotonicity step is stated division-free: if
$S^2\le N(S+c)$ and $u\le S$ then $u^2\le N(u+c)$, proved by clearing
denominators over $\mathbb Z$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Fisher-type counting bound]\label{thm:fisher}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:corradi}, with $t\le m$ and $N=|U|$,
$\;k(m^2-Nt)\le N(m-t)$. In the design regime $Nt<m^2$ this reads
$k\le N(m-t)/(m^2-Nt)$: large, nearly disjoint sets cannot be numerous.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Expand $N(m+(k-1)t)+Nt=Nm+k(Nt)$ and combine with Theorem~\ref{thm:corradi} to
get $km^2+Nt\le Nm+k(Nt)$; rearrange, using $t\le m$ to handle natural-number
subtraction.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Tightness at $t=0$]\label{thm:t0}
If $|A_i|=m$ for every $i$ and the family is pairwise disjoint, then
$km^2=|U|\cdot(m+(k-1)\cdot 0)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Tightness at $t=m$]\label{thm:tm}
If $I$ is nonempty and $A_i=B$ for every $i$ with $|B|=m$, then
$km^2=|U|\cdot(m+(k-1)m)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}
No bound on $|U|$ expressible as a function of $(k,m,t)$ alone can improve on
Theorem~\ref{thm:corradi} at the endpoints $t\in\{0,m\}$. In the interior, the
triangle of Definition~\ref{def:witness} shows tightness at $(k,m,t)=(3,2,1)$,
while the sunflower---with the same $(k,m,t)$---is strictly above the bound.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Ensemble coverage bound]
Let $H$ be a finite set of hypotheses on a finite sample space, each failing on
at least $m$ samples, with any two failing simultaneously on at most $t$
samples. Then the set of samples on which the ensemble is not unanimously
correct has size at least $|H|m^2/(m+(|H|-1)t)$. When $t=0$ and $m>0$ this
strengthens to $|H|\cdot m\le|U|$.
\end{theorem}

\section{Applications}

\paragraph{Ensemble design and diversity metrics.} The rigidity theorems give
sharp operational meaning to three folklore heuristics. ``Diverse errors are
good'' becomes Theorem~\ref{thm:rig1}: the union bound is lossless iff errors
never co-occur. ``Pairwise diversity is not enough'' becomes
Theorems~\ref{thm:nof} and \ref{thm:threshold}. ``Balanced ensembles are
extremal'' becomes Theorem~\ref{thm:rig4}, stable under perturbation with
modulus $\sqrt g$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:spread}.

\paragraph{Multiple hypothesis testing.} The classical Bonferroni correction is
the first-order truncation; Theorem~\ref{thm:sharpdefect} quantifies the exact
defect of the second-order correction. Where no sample triggers three or more
rejections, the correction is exactly lossless (Theorem~\ref{thm:rig3}).

\paragraph{Design theory and coding.} Theorems~\ref{thm:corradi} and
\ref{thm:fisher} are the standard Corr\'adi and Fisher-type counting principles;
the contribution here is their derivation from the same two moment identities,
and the identification (Theorem~\ref{thm:rig4}) of their extremal families as
exactly the regular covers, i.e.\ as $(k,m,t)$-designs.

\section{Discussion and future work}

\subsection{What is settled}

The Bonferroni machinery is an identity minus an explicit irregularity
functional (Theorems~\ref{thm:defect}, \ref{thm:sharpdefect}). Its extremal
classes are exactly three: pairwise disjoint, multiplicity $\le 2$, and regular
covers (Theorems~\ref{thm:rig1}--\ref{thm:rig4}). Second-order marginals never
determine the union (Theorem~\ref{thm:nof}), marginals of order $<k$ never
determine the union of $k$ sets (Theorem~\ref{thm:threshold}), while all orders
do (Theorem~\ref{thm:incexc}).

\begin{conjecture}[Marginal-order complexity of the union-bound gap]
For every $k$ and every $2\le r<k$ there is a constant $c(r)>0$ such that two
families of $k$ sets agreeing on all marginals of order $\le r$ can have unions
differing by a factor $\ge 1+c(r)$, and $c(r)\to 0$ as $r\to k$: the
quantitative information content of marginal order $r$ degrades smoothly, not
abruptly.
\end{conjecture}

The key insight is that $\delta(S)=(-1)^{k-|S|}$ is only the top M\"obius
eigenvector; the whole family of perturbations supported on the levels above $r$
forms a cone whose extreme rays should control the achievable ratio, turning the
existence statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:threshold} into an extremal problem over
the Boolean lattice.

\begin{conjecture}[Corr\'adi is the exact envelope of the $(k,m,t)$ data]
For all $k,m,t$ with $t\le m$ there exists a family of $k$ sets with all first
marginals exactly $m$ and all second marginals exactly $t$ whose union has
cardinality exactly $\lceil km^2/(m+(k-1)t)\rceil$; consequently
Theorem~\ref{thm:corradi} is not merely a bound but the pointwise minimum of the
union over the marginal class.
\end{conjecture}

The key insight is that Theorem~\ref{thm:rig4} identifies the extremal families
as regular covers, i.e.\ as $(k,m,t)$-designs, so the conjecture is exactly an
asymptotic existence statement for such designs. The two extreme cases $t=0$ and
$t=m$ are already tight (Theorems~\ref{thm:t0}, \ref{thm:tm}), and the rigidity
theorem says precisely which combinatorial object must be built for intermediate
$t$.

\begin{conjecture}[A stability dichotomy with an algebraic threshold]
There is a function $\gamma(k,|U|)$, growing at most polynomially, such that
every family with $0<g<\gamma(k,|U|)$ has multiplicity profile within bounded
Hamming distance of a constant profile: the gap cannot be small unless the
family is a bounded perturbation of a regular cover, with no intermediate regime
of moderately irregular, moderately small-gap families.
\end{conjecture}

Corollary~\ref{cor:hard} is the case $\gamma=1$; the content is to push the
threshold up to a nontrivial function of the parameters.

\subsection{Further directions}

All moment identities hold verbatim with counting measure replaced by an
arbitrary finite measure, the rigidity statements becoming almost-everywhere
statements; the integrality argument of Corollary~\ref{cor:hard} is the only
step that genuinely uses counting. The pattern $(d-1)^2\to(d-1)(d-2)$ suggests a

import math
import random
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple

Family = Sequence[Set[int]]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core multiplicity calculus
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def multiplicity(family: Family) -> Dict[int, int]:
    """Return {x: d(x)} for every covered point x, where d(x) counts the
    members of the family containing x."""
    d: Dict[int, int] = {}
    for member in family:
        for x in member:
            d[x] = d.get(x, 0) + 1
    return d


def cover(family: Family) -> Set[int]:
    """The union of the family."""
    out: Set[int] = set()
    for member in family:
        out |= member
    return out


def double_collision(family: Family) -> Set[int]:
    """Points covered at least twice."""
    return {x for x, dx in multiplicity(family).items() if dx >= 2}


def sigma1(family: Family) -> int:
    """Sum of the first marginals, sum_i |A_i|."""
    return sum(len(member) for member in family)


def sigma2_offdiag(family: Family) -> int:
    """Off-diagonal pairwise-overlap mass, sum_{i != j} |A_i cap A_j|."""
    k = len(family)
    return sum(len(family[i] & family[j])
               for i in range(k) for j in range(k) if i != j)


def sigma2_total(family: Family) -> int:
    """Total ordered pairwise-overlap mass, sum_{i,j} |A_i cap A_j|."""
    k = len(family)
    return sum(len(family[i] & family[j]) for i in range(k) for j in range(k))


def bonferroni_defect(family: Family) -> int:
    """Irregularity functional sum_{x in U} (d(x) - 1)^2."""
    return sum((dx - 1) ** 2 for dx in multiplicity(family).values())


def sharp_defect(family: Family) -> int:
    """Sharp Bonferroni defect sum_{x in U} (d(x) - 1)(d(x) - 2)."""
    return sum((dx - 1) * (dx - 2) for dx in multiplicity(family).values())


def cs_gap(family: Family) -> int:
    """Cauchy-Schwarz gap g = |U| * S2tot - S1^2 (a nonnegative integer)."""
    return len(cover(family)) * sigma2_total(family) - sigma1(family) ** 2


def is_regular(family: Family) -> bool:
    """True iff the multiplicity is constant on the cover."""
    values = set(multiplicity(family).values())
    return len(values) <= 1


def is_pairwise_disjoint(family: Family) -> bool:
    k = len(family)
    return all(not (family[i] & family[j])
               for i in range(k) for j in range(k) if i != j)


def max_multiplicity(family: Family) -> int:
    d = multiplicity(family)
    return max(d.values()) if d else 0


def joint_marginal(family: Family, T: Iterable[int]) -> int:
    """|intersection over i in T of A_i|; the empty T is not used here."""
    idx = list(T)
    if not idx:
        raise ValueError("joint_marginal requires a nonempty subfamily")
    out = set(family[idx[0]])
    for i in idx[1:]:
        out &= family[i]
    return len(out)


def inclusion_exclusion_union(family: Family) -> int:
    """|U| recomputed from all joint marginals via inclusion-exclusion."""
    k = len(family)
    total = 0
    for r in range(1, k + 1):
        for T in itertools.combinations(range(k), r):
            total += (-1) ** (r + 1) * joint_marginal(family, T)
    return total

# Corradi's inequality
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def corradi_data(family: Family) -> Tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    """Return (k, m, t, |U|) with m the min first marginal and t the max
    off-diagonal second marginal."""
    k = len(family)
    m = min(len(member) for member in family) if k else 0
    t = max((len(family[i] & family[j])
             for i in range(k) for j in range(k) if i != j), default=0)
    return k, m, t, len(cover(family))


def corradi_check(name: str, family: Family) -> None:
    k, m, t, N = corradi_data(family)
    lhs = k * m * m
    rhs = N * (m + (k - 1) * t)
    status = "TIGHT" if lhs == rhs else "strict"
    bound = lhs / (m + (k - 1) * t) if (m + (k - 1) * t) else float("inf")
    print(f"  {name:<26} k={k} m={m} t={t} |U|={N}: "
          f"{lhs} <= {rhs}  [{status}]   |U| >= {bound:.4f}")
    assert lhs <= rhs, name

    second_sun = {(i, j): len(SUNFLOWER[i] & SUNFLOWER[j])
                  for i in range(3) for j in range(3)}

    print(f"  second marginals identical: {second_tri == second_sun}")

    print(f"  |U| sunflower = {len(cover(SUNFLOWER))}")
    check("identical first marginals", first_tri == first_sun)
    check("identical second marginals", second_tri == second_sun)
    check("different unions",

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The parity construction: order < k is never enough
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def parity_construction(k: int) -> Tuple[List[Set[int]], List[Set[int]]]:
    """Build the plain and parity families of k sets on the ground set
    P({0,...,k-1}) x {0,1}, encoded as integers.

    Ground point (S, b) is encoded as the integer 2 * bitmask(S) + b.
    plain_i  = {(S, 0) : i in S}
    parity_i = {(S, b) : i in S, |S| = k (mod 2)}
    """
    plain: List[Set[int]] = [set() for _ in range(k)]
    parity: List[Set[int]] = [set() for _ in range(k)]
    for mask in range(1 << k):
        size = bin(mask).count("1")
        right_parity = (size + k) % 2 == 0
        for i in range(k):
            if mask >> i & 1:
                plain[i].add(2 * mask)
                if right_parity:
                    parity[i].add(2 * mask)
                    parity[i].add(2 * mask + 1)
    return plain, parity


def demo_marginal_threshold(kmax: int = 6) -> None:
    print("\n" + "=" * 74)
    print("MARGINAL-ORDER THRESHOLD: ORDER < k NEVER DETERMINES THE UNION")
    print("=" * 74)
    print(f"  {'k':>2} {'|U| plain':>10} {'|U| parity':>11} "
          f"{'orders <k agree':>16} {'top order':>18}")
    for k in range(1, kmax + 1):
        plain, parity = parity_construction(k)
        agree = True
        for r in range(1, k):
            for T in itertools.combinations(range(k), r):
                if joint_marginal(plain, T) != joint_marginal(parity, T):
                    agree = False
        top_p = joint_marginal(plain, range(k))
        top_q = joint_marginal(parity, range(k))
        up, uq = len(cover(plain)), len(cover(parity))
        print(f"  {k:>2} {up:>10} {uq:>11} {str(agree):>16} "
              f"{f'{top_p} vs {top_q}':>18}")
        check(f"k={k}: all marginals of order < k agree", agree)
        check(f"k={k}: top-order marginals differ", top_p != top_q)
        check(f"k={k}: unions differ", up != uq)
        check(f"k={k}: plain cover is 2^k - 1", up == (1 << k) - 1)
        check(f"k={k}: parity cover is even", uq % 2 == 0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Corradi tightness at both ends of the correlation scale
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_corradi() -> None:
    print("\n" + "=" * 74)
    print("CORRADI'S INEQUALITY  k m^2 <= |U| (m + (k-1) t)")
    print("=" * 74)

    # t = 0 : pairwise disjoint m-sets  -> TIGHT

    disjoint = [set(range(i * m, (i + 1) * m)) for i in range(k)]
    corradi_check("disjoint (t = 0)", disjoint)

    # t = m : all members equal        -> TIGHT
    identical = [set(range(m)) for _ in range(k)]
    corradi_check("identical (t = m)", identical)

    # interior tight example: the triangle (a regular cover)
    corradi_check("triangle (regular)", TRIANGLE)

    # interior strict example: the sunflower, SAME (k, m, t)
    corradi_check("sunflower (irregular)", SUNFLOWER)

    print("  Triangle and sunflower share (k,m,t) = (3,2,1); the regular one is")
    print("  tight and the irregular one is strict -- exactly as rigidity predicts.")

    print("\n  Fisher-type bound  k (m^2 - N t) <= N (m - t)  in the design regime:")
    for fam, label in ((disjoint, "disjoint"), (TRIANGLE, "triangle")):
        k, m, t, N = corradi_data(fam)
        if t <= m and N * t < m * m:

            rhs = N * (m - t)
            print(f"    {label:<10} k={k} m={m} t={t} N={N}: {lhs} <= {rhs}")
            assert lhs <= rhs
        else:
            print(f"    {label:<10} k={k} m={m} t={t} N={N}: "
                  f"outside the design regime (N t = {N * t} >= m^2 = {m * m})")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Randomised stress test
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def random_family(rng: random.Random, k: int, n: int) -> List[Set[int]]:
    return [set(x for x in range(n) if rng.random() < 0.4) for _ in range(k)]


def demo_random_stress(trials: int = 3000, seed: int = 20260818) -> None:
    print("\n" + "=" * 74)
    print(f"RANDOMISED STRESS TEST ({trials} random families)")
    print("=" * 74)
    rng = random.Random(seed)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main() -> None:
    print("=" * 74)
    print("MULTIPLICITY CALCULUS FOR FINITE FAMILIES -- NUMERICAL DEMONSTRATION")
    print("=" * 74)

    return len(cover(family)) * sigma2_total(family) - sigma1(family) ** 2


def is_regular(family: Family) -> bool:
    """True iff the multiplicity is constant on the cover."""
    values = set(multiplicity(family).values())
    return len(values) <= 1


def is_pairwise_disjoint(family: Family) -> bool:
    k = len(family)
    return all(not (family[i] & family[j])
               for i in range(k) for j in range(k) if i != j)


def max_multiplicity(family: Family) -> int:
    d = multiplicity(family)
    return max(d.values()) if d else 0


def joint_marginal(family: Family, T: Iterable[int]) -> int:
    """|intersection over i in T of A_i|; the empty T is not used here."""
    idx = list(T)
    if not idx:
        raise ValueError("joint_marginal requires a nonempty subfamily")
    out = set(family[idx[0]])
    for i in idx[1:]:
        out &= family[i]
    return len(out)


def inclusion_exclusion_union(family: Family) -> int:
    """|U| recomputed from all joint marginals via inclusion-exclusion."""
    k = len(family)
    total = 0
    for r in range(1, k + 1):
        for T in itertools.combinations(range(k), r):
            total += (-1) ** (r + 1) * joint_marginal(family, T)
    return total

    mark = "OK " if condition else "FAIL"
    line = f"  [{mark}] {label}"

def report(name: str, family: Family) -> None:
    """Print the full second-order dossier of a family and verify every
    identity and inequality of the theory on it."""
    U = cover(family)
    d = multiplicity(family)
    S1 = sigma1(family)
    S2 = sigma2_offdiag(family)
    S2t = sigma2_total(family)
    D = double_collision(family)
    g = cs_gap(family)
    profile = sorted((d[x] for x in U), reverse=True)

    print(f"\n=== {name} ===")
    print(f"  members            : {[sorted(m) for m in family]}")
    print(f"  |A_i|              : {[len(m) for m in family]}")
    print(f"  cover U            : {sorted(U)}   |U| = {len(U)}")
    print(f"  multiplicity profile: {profile}")
    print(f"  S1 = sum |A_i|     : {S1}")
    print(f"  S2 = offdiag mass  : {S2}")
    print(f"  S2tot (with diag)  : {S2t}")
    print(f"  |D| (double coll.) : {len(D)}  -> D = {sorted(D)}")
    print(f"  Bonferroni defect  : {bonferroni_defect(family)}")
    print(f"  sharp defect       : {sharp_defect(family)}")
    print(f"  Cauchy-Schwarz gap : {g}")

    # ---- moment identities
    check("first moment identity  sum_U d = S1",
          sum(d[x] for x in U) == S1,
          f"{sum(d[x] for x in U)} = {S1}")
    check("second moment identity sum_U d^2 = S2tot",
          sum(d[x] ** 2 for x in U) == S2t,
          f"{sum(d[x] ** 2 for x in U)} = {S2t}")
    check("off-diagonal identity  S2 = sum_U d(d-1)",
          sum(d[x] * (d[x] - 1) for x in U) == S2,
          f"{sum(d[x] * (d[x] - 1) for x in U)} = {S2}")

    # ---- defect identities
    check("Bonferroni defect identity  S1 + Irr = |U| + S2",
          S1 + bonferroni_defect(family) == len(U) + S2,
          f"{S1} + {bonferroni_defect(family)} = {len(U)} + {S2}")
    check("sharp defect identity  2 S1 + sharpIrr = 2|U| + S2",
          2 * S1 + sharp_defect(family) == 2 * len(U) + S2,
          f"{2 * S1} + {sharp_defect(family)} = {2 * len(U)} + {S2}")

    # ---- inequalities
    check("second Bonferroni  S1 <= |U| + S2", S1 <= len(U) + S2,
          f"{S1} <= {len(U) + S2}")
    check("sharp Bonferroni   2 S1 <= 2|U| + S2", 2 * S1 <= 2 * len(U) + S2,
          f"{2 * S1} <= {2 * len(U) + S2}")
    check("double collision   2|D| <= S2", 2 * len(D) <= S2,
          f"{2 * len(D)} <= {S2}")
    check("Cauchy-Schwarz     S1^2 <= |U| S2tot", S1 ** 2 <= len(U) * S2t,
          f"{S1 ** 2} <= {len(U) * S2t}")
    check("gap nonnegative", g >= 0, f"g = {g}")

    # ---- rigidity
    check("rigidity I:  Bonferroni tight  <=>  pairwise disjoint",
          (S1 == len(U) + S2) == is_pairwise_disjoint(family))
    check("rigidity II: sharp tight  <=>  double-collision tight  <=>  d <= 2",
          (2 * S1 == 2 * len(U) + S2)
          == (2 * len(D) == S2)
          == (max_multiplicity(family) <= 2))
    check("rigidity III: Cauchy-Schwarz tight  <=>  regular cover",
          (S1 ** 2 == len(U) * S2t) == is_regular(family))

    # ---- stability
    if U:
        worst = max((d[x] - d[y]) ** 2 for x in U for y in U)
        check("stability: max (d(x)-d(y))^2 <= g", worst <= g,
              f"{worst} <= {g}")
        check("integrality: g < 1  =>  regular", (g >= 1) or is_regular(family))
        if S1 == len(U):
            check("defect-gap link: |U| * Irr = g  (average multiplicity 1)",
                  len(U) * bonferroni_defect(family) == g)

    # ---- inclusion-exclusion consistency
    check("inclusion-exclusion reproduces |U|",
          inclusion_exclusion_union(family) == len(U),
          f"{inclusion_exclusion_union(family)} = {len(U)}")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Corradi's inequality
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def corradi_data(family: Family) -> Tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    """Return (k, m, t, |U|) with m the min first marginal and t the max
    off-diagonal second marginal."""
    k = len(family)
    m = min(len(member) for member in family) if k else 0
    t = max((len(family[i] & family[j])
             for i in range(k) for j in range(k) if i != j), default=0)
    return k, m, t, len(cover(family))


def corradi_check(name: str, family: Family) -> None:
    k, m, t, N = corradi_data(family)
    lhs = k * m * m
    rhs = N * (m + (k - 1) * t)
    status = "TIGHT" if lhs == rhs else "strict"
    bound = lhs / (m + (k - 1) * t) if (m + (k - 1) * t) else float("inf")
    print(f"  {name:<26} k={k} m={m} t={t} |U|={N}: "
          f"{lhs} <= {rhs}  [{status}]   |U| >= {bound:.4f}")
    assert lhs <= rhs, name

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The parity construction: order < k is never enough
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def parity_construction(k: int) -> Tuple[List[Set[int]], List[Set[int]]]:
    """Build the plain and parity families of k sets on the ground set
    P({0,...,k-1}) x {0,1}, encoded as integers.

    Ground point (S, b) is encoded as the integer 2 * bitmask(S) + b.
    plain_i  = {(S, 0) : i in S}
    parity_i = {(S, b) : i in S, |S| = k (mod 2)}
    """
    plain: List[Set[int]] = [set() for _ in range(k)]
    parity: List[Set[int]] = [set() for _ in range(k)]
    for mask in range(1 << k):
        size = bin(mask).count("1")
        right_parity = (size + k) % 2 == 0
        for i in range(k):
            if mask >> i & 1:
                plain[i].add(2 * mask)
                if right_parity:
                    parity[i].add(2 * mask)
                    parity[i].add(2 * mask + 1)
    return plain, parity


def demo_marginal_threshold(kmax: int = 6) -> None:
    print("\n" + "=" * 74)
    print("MARGINAL-ORDER THRESHOLD: ORDER < k NEVER DETERMINES THE UNION")
    print("=" * 74)
    print(f"  {'k':>2} {'|U| plain':>10} {'|U| parity':>11} "
          f"{'orders <k agree':>16} {'top order':>18}")
    for k in range(1, kmax + 1):
        plain, parity = parity_construction(k)
        agree = True
        for r in range(1, k):
            for T in itertools.combinations(range(k), r):
                if joint_marginal(plain, T) != joint_marginal(parity, T):
                    agree = False
        top_p = joint_marginal(plain, range(k))
        top_q = joint_marginal(parity, range(k))
        up, uq = len(cover(plain)), len(cover(parity))
        print(f"  {k:>2} {up:>10} {uq:>11} {str(agree):>16} "
              f"{f'{top_p} vs {top_q}':>18}")
        check(f"k={k}: all marginals of order < k agree", agree)
        check(f"k={k}: top-order marginals differ", top_p != top_q)
        check(f"k={k}: unions differ", up != uq)
        check(f"k={k}: plain cover is 2^k - 1", up == (1 << k) - 1)
        check(f"k={k}: parity cover is even", uq % 2 == 0)

def demo_corradi() -> None:
    print("\n" + "=" * 74)
    print("CORRADI'S INEQUALITY  k m^2 <= |U| (m + (k-1) t)")
    print("=" * 74)

    # t = 0 : pairwise disjoint m-sets  -> TIGHT
    k, m = 4, 3
    disjoint = [set(range(i * m, (i + 1) * m)) for i in range(k)]
    corradi_check("disjoint (t = 0)", disjoint)

    # t = m : all members equal        -> TIGHT
    identical = [set(range(m)) for _ in range(k)]
    corradi_check("identical (t = m)", identical)

    # interior tight example: the triangle (a regular cover)
    corradi_check("triangle (regular)", TRIANGLE)

    # interior strict example: the sunflower, SAME (k, m, t)
    corradi_check("sunflower (irregular)", SUNFLOWER)

    print("  Triangle and sunflower share (k,m,t) = (3,2,1); the regular one is")
    print("  tight and the irregular one is strict -- exactly as rigidity predicts.")

    print("\n  Fisher-type bound  k (m^2 - N t) <= N (m - t)  in the design regime:")
    for fam, label in ((disjoint, "disjoint"), (TRIANGLE, "triangle")):
        k, m, t, N = corradi_data(fam)
        if t <= m and N * t < m * m:
            lhs = k * (m * m - N * t)
            rhs = N * (m - t)
            print(f"    {label:<10} k={k} m={m} t={t} N={N}: {lhs} <= {rhs}")
            assert lhs <= rhs
        else:
            print(f"    {label:<10} k={k} m={m} t={t} N={N}: "
                  f"outside the design regime (N t = {N * t} >= m^2 = {m * m})")

def random_family(rng: random.Random, k: int, n: int) -> List[Set[int]]:
    return [set(x for x in range(n) if rng.random() < 0.4) for _ in range(k)]


def demo_random_stress(trials: int = 3000, seed: int = 20260818) -> None:
    print("\n" + "=" * 74)
    print(f"RANDOMISED STRESS TEST ({trials} random families)")
    print("=" * 74)
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    tight_bonf = tight_sharp = tight_cs = 0
    worst_spread_ratio = 0.0
    for _ in range(trials):
        k = rng.randint(1, 5)
        n = rng.randint(1, 8)
        fam = random_family(rng, k, n)
        U = cover(fam)
        d = multiplicity(fam)
        S1, S2, S2t = sigma1(fam), sigma2_offdiag(fam), sigma2_total(fam)
        g = cs_gap(fam)

        assert S1 + bonferroni_defect(fam) == len(U) + S2
        assert 2 * S1 + sharp_defect(fam) == 2 * len(U) + S2
        assert 2 * len(double_collision(fam)) <= S2
        assert S1 ** 2 <= len(U) * S2t
        assert g >= 0
        assert inclusion_exclusion_union(fam) == len(U)
        assert (S1 == len(U) + S2) == is_pairwise_disjoint(fam)
        assert ((2 * S1 == 2 * len(U) + S2)
                == (max_multiplicity(fam) <= 2))
        assert (S1 ** 2 == len(U) * S2t) == is_regular(fam)
        for x in U:
            for y in U:
                assert (d[x] - d[y]) ** 2 <= g
        if g < 1:
            assert is_regular(fam)

        if U:
            spread = max(d.values()) - min(d.values())
            if g > 0:
                worst_spread_ratio = max(worst_spread_ratio,
                                         spread / math.sqrt(g))
        tight_bonf += S1 == len(U) + S2
        tight_sharp += 2 * S1 == 2 * len(U) + S2
        tight_cs += S1 ** 2 == len(U) * S2t

    print("  all identities, inequalities, rigidity and stability claims hold.")
    print(f"  Bonferroni-tight (disjoint)      : {tight_bonf}/{trials}")
    print(f"  sharp-tight (multiplicity <= 2)  : {tight_sharp}/{trials}")
    print(f"  Cauchy-Schwarz-tight (regular)   : {tight_cs}/{trials}")
    print(f"  worst observed spread / sqrt(g)  : {worst_spread_ratio:.4f}  (<= 1)")
    assert worst_spread_ratio <= 1.0 + 1e-12

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, List, NamedTuple, Sequence, Set

Family = Sequence[Set[int]]


class Dossier(NamedTuple):
    """Complete first- and second-order description of a finite family."""
    k: int                       # number of members
    cover_size: int              # |U|
    profile: Dict[int, int]      # x -> d(x), restricted to the cover
    sigma1: int                  # sum_i |A_i|
    sigma2_offdiag: int          # sum_{i != j} |A_i cap A_j|
    sigma2_total: int            # sum_{i,j} |A_i cap A_j|
    double_collisions: int       # |{x : d(x) >= 2}|
    bonferroni_defect: int       # sum_x (d(x) - 1)^2
    sharp_defect: int            # sum_x (d(x) - 1)(d(x) - 2)
    cs_gap: int                  # |U| * sigma2_total - sigma1^2


def build_dossier(family: Family) -> Dossier:
    """Compute the full second-order dossier of a finite family in one pass.

    Complexity: let k = |I| and s = sum_i |A_i| be the total incidence count.
    Building the multiplicity map is O(s).  The off-diagonal mass is obtained
    from the multiplicity map by the factorial-moment identity
    sum_{i != j} |A_i cap A_j| = sum_x d(x)(d(x) - 1), costing O(|U|) rather
    than the naive O(k^2 * max|A_i|) pairwise-intersection loop.  Total cost
    O(s + |U|) time and O(|U|) space -- linear in the input size, and
    independent of k^2.
    """
    mult: Dict[int, int] = {}
    sigma1 = 0
    for member in family:
        sigma1 += len(member)
        for x in member:
            mult[x] = mult.get(x, 0) + 1

    cover_size = len(mult)
    s2_off = sum(d * (d - 1) for d in mult.values())
    s2_tot = s2_off + sigma1
    return Dossier(
        k=len(family),
        cover_size=cover_size,
        profile=dict(mult),
        sigma1=sigma1,
        sigma2_offdiag=s2_off,
        sigma2_total=s2_tot,
        double_collisions=sum(1 for d in mult.values() if d >= 2),
        bonferroni_defect=sum((d - 1) ** 2 for d in mult.values()),
        sharp_defect=sum((d - 1) * (d - 2) for d in mult.values()),
        cs_gap=cover_size * s2_tot - sigma1 ** 2,
    )


def verify_dossier(family: Family, dossier: Dossier) -> List[str]:
    """Cross-check the dossier against the naive O(k^2) definitions."""
    k = len(family)
    naive_off = sum(len(family[i] & family[j])
                    for i in range(k) for j in range(k) if i != j)
    naive_cover: Set[int] = set()
    for member in family:
        naive_cover |= member
    problems: List[str] = []
    if naive_off != dossier.sigma2_offdiag:
        problems.append("off-diagonal mass mismatch")
    if len(naive_cover) != dossier.cover_size:
        problems.append("cover size mismatch")
    if (dossier.sigma1 + dossier.bonferroni_defect
            != dossier.cover_size + dossier.sigma2_offdiag):
        problems.append("Bonferroni defect identity violated")
    if (2 * dossier.sigma1 + dossier.sharp_defect
            != 2 * dossier.cover_size + dossier.sigma2_offdiag):
        problems.append("sharp defect identity violated")
    if dossier.cs_gap < 0:
        problems.append("Cauchy-Schwarz gap negative")
    return problems

from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple

Family = Sequence[Set[int]]


def multiplicity(family: Family) -> Dict[int, int]:
    mult: Dict[int, int] = {}
    for member in family:
        for x in member:
            mult[x] = mult.get(x, 0) + 1
    return mult


def classify_extremality(family: Family) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Decide, for each of the four second-order bounds, whether the family is
    extremal, and return the exact slack of each.

    Mathematical basis.  Each bound is an identity minus a nonnegative defect:

        Bonferroni        S1 + sum_x (d-1)^2      = |U| + S2
        sharp Bonferroni  2 S1 + sum_x (d-1)(d-2) = 2|U| + S2
        double collision  S2 - 2|D| = sum_x [d(d-1) - 2*(d >= 2)]
        Cauchy-Schwarz    |U| S2tot - S1^2 = (1/2) sum_{x,y} (d(x)-d(y))^2

    Hence extremality is decided purely by the multiplicity profile:
      * Bonferroni tight        <=>  d == 1 everywhere  <=> pairwise disjoint
      * sharp / double-collision tight <=>  d <= 2 everywhere
      * Cauchy-Schwarz tight    <=>  d constant on the cover (regular cover)

    Complexity: O(s + |U|) where s = sum_i |A_i|; a single pass to build the
    multiplicity map, then O(|U|) arithmetic.  No pairwise intersections are
    ever formed.
    """
    mult = multiplicity(family)
    cover_size = len(mult)
    sigma1 = sum(len(m) for m in family)
    s2_off = sum(d * (d - 1) for d in mult.values())
    s2_tot = s2_off + sigma1
    n_double = sum(1 for d in mult.values() if d >= 2)
    values = set(mult.values())

    bonf_defect = sum((d - 1) ** 2 for d in mult.values())
    sharp_def = sum((d - 1) * (d - 2) for d in mult.values())
    gap = cover_size * s2_tot - sigma1 ** 2
    spread = (max(values) - min(values)) if values else 0

    return {
        "profile_multiset": sorted(mult.values(), reverse=True),
        "pairwise_disjoint": values <= {1},
        "multiplicity_at_most_two": all(d <= 2 for d in values),
        "regular_cover": len(values) <= 1,
        "bonferroni_slack": (cover_size + s2_off) - sigma1,
        "bonferroni_defect": bonf_defect,
        "sharp_bonferroni_slack": (2 * cover_size + s2_off) - 2 * sigma1,
        "sharp_defect": sharp_def,
        "double_collision_slack": s2_off - 2 * n_double,
        "cauchy_schwarz_gap": gap,
        "multiplicity_spread": spread,
        "spread_certificate_ok": spread ** 2 <= gap,
        "recommended_bound": _recommend(values),
    }


def _recommend(values: Set[int]) -> str:
    """Which of the three bounds is exactly lossless for this family?"""
    if values <= {1}:
        return "union bound (pairwise disjoint: all three are tight)"
    if len(values) <= 1:
        return "Cauchy-Schwarz / Corradi (regular cover: exactly tight)"
    if all(d <= 2 for d in values):
        return "sharp Bonferroni / double collision (multiplicity <= 2: tight)"
    return "no second-order bound is tight; use the exact defect identities"


def slack_table(families: Sequence[Tuple[str, Family]]) -> List[str]:
    """Human-readable comparison table of slacks across several families."""
    rows = [f"{'family':<24}{'Bonf':>6}{'sharp':>7}{'dblcol':>8}{'gap':>7}  verdict"]
    for name, fam in families:
        c = classify_extremality(fam)
        rows.append(
            f"{name:<24}{c['bonferroni_slack']:>6}{c['sharp_bonferroni_slack']:>7}"
            f"{c['double_collision_slack']:>8}{c['cauchy_schwarz_gap']:>7}  "
            f"{c['recommended_bound']}")
    return rows

from __future__ import annotations

from math import ceil
from typing import List, NamedTuple, Optional


class Envelope(NamedTuple):
    k: int
    m: int
    t: int
    union_lower_bound: float      # k m^2 / (m + (k-1) t)
    union_lower_bound_int: int    # ceiling of the above
    max_sets_given_N: Optional[int]   # Fisher-type cap, if the regime applies
    endpoint_tight: bool          # exactly attainable by an explicit family?


def corradi_envelope(k: int, m: int, t: int,
                     ambient: Optional[int] = None) -> Envelope:
    """Evaluate the second-order marginal envelope for the data (k, m, t).

    Given k sets with all first marginals at least m and all pairwise second
    marginals at most t, the second-moment (Cauchy-Schwarz) bound yields

        k m^2 <= |U| * (m + (k-1) t),      i.e.   |U| >= k m^2 / (m + (k-1) t).

    Turned around, if the union lives in N points and N t < m^2 (the design
    regime) then k (m^2 - N t) <= N (m - t), so

        k <= N (m - t) / (m^2 - N t).

    The bound is attained at both ends of the correlation scale: at t = 0 by a
    pairwise-disjoint family of m-sets (|U| = k m) and at t = m by k copies of a
    single m-set (|U| = m).  Interior tightness holds exactly for regular
    covers.

    Complexity: O(1) arithmetic; the routine is an evaluator, not a search.
    """
    if k <= 0 or m < 0 or t < 0:
        raise ValueError("require k > 0 and m, t >= 0")
    denom = m + (k - 1) * t
    lb = float(k * m * m) / denom if denom else 0.0
    cap: Optional[int] = None
    if ambient is not None and t <= m and ambient * t < m * m:
        cap = (ambient * (m - t)) // (m * m - ambient * t)
    return Envelope(
        k=k, m=m, t=t,
        union_lower_bound=lb,
        union_lower_bound_int=int(ceil(lb - 1e-12)),
        max_sets_given_N=cap,
        endpoint_tight=(t == 0 or t == m),
    )


def envelope_curve(k: int, m: int) -> List[Envelope]:
    """The whole correlation scale t = 0, 1, ..., m for fixed (k, m)."""
    return [corradi_envelope(k, m, t) for t in range(m + 1)]


def certify_family_against_envelope(union_size: int, k: int, m: int,
                                    t: int) -> str:
    """Report where a measured family sits relative to the envelope."""
    env = corradi_envelope(k, m, t)
    if union_size < env.union_lower_bound - 1e-9:
        return "IMPOSSIBLE: measured union below the envelope"
    if abs(union_size - env.union_lower_bound) < 1e-9:
        return "EXTREMAL: regular cover, Corradi exactly tight"
    excess = union_size / env.union_lower_bound
    return f"feasible; union exceeds the envelope by a factor {excess:.4f}"

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
from typing import Dict, List, Set, Tuple

Family = List[Set[int]]


def parity_pair(k: int) -> Tuple[Family, Family]:
    """Construct the two k-set families that are indistinguishable below order k.

    Ground set: P({0,...,k-1}) x {first, second}, encoded as integers
    2 * bitmask + bit, so |Omega| = 2^(k+1).

        plain_i  = {(S, first)          : i in S}
        parity_i = {(S, first),(S,second): i in S and |S| = k (mod 2)}

    Reading each family as a weight function on subsets -- w(S) = number of
    ground points over S -- the plain family has w = 1 and the parity family has
    w = 1 + (-1)^(k - |S|).  The perturbation delta(S) = (-1)^(k - |S|) is the
    top Mobius eigenvector of the Boolean lattice: all of its upper sums
    sum_{S superset T} delta(S) vanish for T a proper subset, by the alternating
    binomial identity, while the top one equals 1.  Hence all joint marginals of
    order < k agree, the order-k marginal differs (1 vs 2), and the unions
    differ (2^k - 1, odd, versus an even number).

    Complexity: O(k * 2^k) to build both families; verification of all marginals
    of order < k costs O(2^k * k) intersections in the worst case, so the
    verifier is exponential in k by necessity -- it inspects every subfamily.
    """
    plain: Family = [set() for _ in range(k)]
    parity: Family = [set() for _ in range(k)]
    for mask in range(1 << k):
        size = bin(mask).count("1")
        right_parity = (size + k) % 2 == 0
        for i in range(k):
            if mask >> i & 1:
                plain[i].add(2 * mask)
                if right_parity:
                    parity[i].add(2 * mask)
                    parity[i].add(2 * mask + 1)
    return plain, parity


def joint_marginal(family: Family, T: Tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
    """|intersection_{i in T} A_i| for a nonempty index tuple T."""
    out = set(family[T[0]])
    for i in T[1:]:
        out &= family[i]
    return len(out)


def cover_size(family: Family) -> int:
    out: Set[int] = set()
    for member in family:
        out |= member
    return len(out)


def verify_indistinguishability(k: int) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Check every claim of the construction for a given k."""
    plain, parity = parity_pair(k)
    disagreements: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
    for r in range(1, k):
        for T in itertools.combinations(range(k), r):
            if joint_marginal(plain, T) != joint_marginal(parity, T):
                disagreements.append(T)
    top = tuple(range(k))
    return {
        "k": k,
        "ground_set_size": 1 << (k + 1),
        "low_order_disagreements": disagreements,
        "all_low_orders_agree": not disagreements,
        "top_marginal_plain": joint_marginal(plain, top),
        "top_marginal_parity": joint_marginal(parity, top),
        "cover_plain": cover_size(plain),
        "cover_parity": cover_size(parity),
        "unions_differ": cover_size(plain) != cover_size(parity),
    }


def mobius_upper_sums(k: int) -> Dict[int, int]:
    """Upper sums of delta(S) = (-1)^(k-|S|) grouped by |T|, over all T.

    Every entry must be 0 except for |T| = k, where it is 1: this is the
    algebraic heart of the construction.
    """
    sums: Dict[int, int] = {}
    for tmask in range(1 << k):
        tot = 0
        for smask in range(1 << k):
            if smask & tmask == tmask:      # S superset T
                tot += (-1) ** ((k - bin(smask).count("1")) % 2)
        size = bin(tmask).count("1")
        if size in sums and sums[size] != tot:
            sums[size] = None  # type: ignore[assignment]
        else:
            sums[size] = tot
    return sums

              f"covers {info['cover_plain']} vs {info['cover_parity']}")
    print("\nMobius upper sums of delta by |T| (k = 5):", mobius_upper_sums(5))

def fisher_cap(N: float, m: float, t: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    denom = m * m - N * t

      "code": """"Visualization 3: The stability certificate  spread <= sqrt(gap).

Samples many random finite families, computes for each one

    gap    g      = |U| * sum_{i,j} |A_i cap A_j| - (sum_i |A_i|)^2
    spread        = max_{x in U} d(x) - min_{x in U} d(x)

and plots spread against sqrt(g).  Every point must lie on or below the
diagonal spread = sqrt(g); the families sitting exactly on the axis
spread = 0 are precisely the regular covers, which are exactly the families
attaining the Cauchy-Schwarz bound.  The integrality gap 0 < g < 1 is empty,
which is why the region between the origin and g = 1 contains no irregular
family.

"""

from __future__ import annotations

import random
from typing import Dict, List, Set, Tuple

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def multiplicity(family: List[Set[int]]) -> Dict[int, int]:
    mult: Dict[int, int] = {}
    for member in family:
        for x in member:
            mult[x] = mult.get(x, 0) + 1
    return mult


def gap_and_spread(family: List[Set[int]]) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    mult = multiplicity(family)
    if not mult:
        return 0, 0
    s1 = sum(len(m) for m in family)
    s2_tot = sum(d * (d - 1) for d in mult.values()) + s1
    gap = len(mult) * s2_tot - s1 * s1
    spread = max(mult.values()) - min(mult.values())
    return gap, spread


def sample(rng: random.Random, trials: int = 4000
           ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    gaps: List[int] = []
    spreads: List[int] = []
    regular: List[bool] = []
    for _ in range(trials):
        k = rng.randint(2, 7)
        n = rng.randint(2, 12)
        p = rng.uniform(0.15, 0.85)
        fam = [set(x for x in range(n) if rng.random() < p) for _ in range(k)]
        if not any(fam):
            continue
        g, s = gap_and_spread(fam)
        gaps.append(g)
        spreads.append(s)
        regular.append(s == 0)
    return np.array(gaps), np.array(spreads), np.array(regular)


def main() -> None:
    rng = random.Random(20260818)
    gaps, spreads, regular = sample(rng)
    root = np.sqrt(gaps.astype(float))

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.0, 6.2))
    ax.scatter(root[~regular], spreads[~regular], s=10, alpha=0.35,
               color="#3b6ea5", label="irregular families")
    ax.scatter(root[regular], spreads[regular], s=18, alpha=0.8,
               color="#6aa84f", label="regular covers (Cauchy-Schwarz tight)")

    xmax = float(root.max()) * 1.05 if len(root) else 1.0
    xs = np.linspace(0, xmax, 200)
    ax.plot(xs, xs, color="#c94f4f", lw=2,
            label=r"certificate  spread $=\sqrt{g}$")
    ax.axvline(1.0, color="black", ls=":", lw=1.2,
               label="integrality threshold  g = 1")

    violations = int(np.sum(spreads ** 2 > gaps))
    ax.set_xlabel(r"$\sqrt{g}$   (square root of the Cauchy-Schwarz gap)")
    ax.set_ylabel("multiplicity spread  max d  -  min d")
    ax.set_title("Stability: the multiplicity spread never exceeds the square\n"
                 f"root of the gap  ({len(gaps)} random families, "
                 f"{violations} violations)")
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax.legend()
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("stability_certificate.png", dpi=160)
    print(f"wrote stability_certificate.png  (violations: {violations})")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

<script>
let ROWS = 3, COLS = 4;
let M = [];

const PRESETS = {
  triangle:  {r:3,c:4,cells:[[0,1],[1,2],[2,0]]},
  sunflower: {r:3,c:4,cells:[[0,1],[0,2],[0,3]]},
  partition: {r:3,c:6,cells:[[0,1],[2,3],[4,5]]},
  identical: {r:3,c:4,cells:[[0,1,2],[0,1,2],[0,1,2]]},
  quad:      {r:4,c:6,cells:[[0,1,2],[2,3,4],[4,5,0],[0,2,4]]},
  empty:     {r:3,c:4,cells:[[],[],[]]}
};

function blank(r,c){ return Array.from({length:r},()=>Array(c).fill(0)); }

function preset(name){
  const p = PRESETS[name];
  ROWS = p.r; COLS = p.c;
  M = blank(ROWS, COLS);
  p.cells.forEach((row,i)=>row.forEach(j=>{ if(j<COLS) M[i][j]=1; }));

function addRow(){ if(ROWS<8){ ROWS++; M.push(Array(COLS).fill(0)); render(); } }
function delRow(){ if(ROWS>1){ ROWS--; M.pop(); render(); } }
function addCol(){ if(COLS<14){ COLS++; M.forEach(r=>r.push(0)); render(); } }
function delCol(){ if(COLS>1){ COLS--; M.forEach(r=>r.pop()); render(); } }
function toggle(i,j){ M[i][j]=1-M[i][j]; render(); }

function stats(){
  const d = [];
  for(let j=0;j<COLS;j++){
    let s=0; for(let i=0;i<ROWS;i++) s+=M[i][j];
    d.push(s);
  }
  const covered = d.filter(v=>v>0);
  const U = covered.length;
  const S1 = d.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0);
  const S2 = covered.reduce((a,v)=>a+v*(v-1),0);
  const S2t = S2 + S1;
  const D  = covered.filter(v=>v>=2).length;
  const defect = covered.reduce((a,v)=>a+(v-1)*(v-1),0);
  const sharp  = covered.reduce((a,v)=>a+(v-1)*(v-2),0);
  const gap = U*S2t - S1*S1;
  const mx = covered.length?Math.max(...covered):0;
  const mn = covered.length?Math.min(...covered):0;
  const sizes = M.map(r=>r.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0));
  let t = 0;
  for(let i=0;i<ROWS;i++) for(let j2=0;j2<ROWS;j2++) if(i!==j2){
    let inter=0; for(let c=0;c<COLS;c++) if(M[i][c]&&M[j2][c]) inter++;
    t = Math.max(t, inter);
  }
  return {d,U,S1,S2,S2t,D,defect,sharp,gap,mx,mn,covered,
          m: sizes.length?Math.min(...sizes):0, t, sizes};
}

function bar(value, max, colour){
  const w = max>0 ? Math.max(2, Math.round(240*value/max)) : 2;
  return `<div class="bar" style="width:${w}px;background:${colour}"></div>`;
}

function stackRow(label, parts, total, max){
  const segs = parts.map(p=>
    `<div class="seg" style="flex:${Math.max(p.v,0.001)};background:${p.c}">${p.v>0?p.t:''}</div>`
  ).join('');
  const grow = max>0 ? total/max : 1;
  return `<div class="eq"><span style="width:132px;color:#9aa8c4;font-size:.82rem">${label}</span>
          <div class="stack" style="max-width:${Math.max(12,Math.round(100*grow))}%">${segs}</div>
          <b>${total}</b></div>`;
}

function render(){
  // matrix
  const s = stats();
  let h = '<table class="inc"><tr><th></th>';
  for(let j=0;j<COLS;j++) h += `<th>${j}</th>`;
  h += '</tr>';
  for(let i=0;i<ROWS;i++){
    h += `<tr><th>A${i}</th>`;
    for(let j=0;j<COLS;j++)
      h += `<td class="cell ${M[i][j]?'on':''}" onclick="toggle(${i},${j})">${M[i][j]?'●':''}</td>`;
    h += '</tr>';
  }
  h += '<tr><th>d</th>';
  for(let j=0;j<COLS;j++){
    const v=s.d[j];
    const cls = v===0?'m0':(v===1?'m1':(v===2?'m2':'m3'));
    h += `<td class="mult ${cls}">${v}</td>`;
  }
  h += '</tr></table>';
  document.getElementById('matrix').innerHTML = h;

  // histogram
  const counts = {};
  s.covered.forEach(v=>counts[v]=(counts[v]||0)+1);
  const keys = Object.keys(counts).map(Number).sort((a,b)=>a-b);
  const mxc = keys.length?Math.max(...keys.map(k=>counts[k])):1;
  const cols = {1:'#6ddf9f',2:'#ffc76b'};
  document.getElementById('hist').innerHTML = keys.length
    ? keys.map(k=>`<div class="barrow"><span class="lab">d=${k}</span>
        ${bar(counts[k], mxc, cols[k]||'#ff8080')}<span>${counts[k]}</span></div>`).join('')
    : '<div class="hint">empty family</div>';

  // dossier
  document.getElementById('dossier').innerHTML = `
    <tr><td>number of sets  k</td><td>${ROWS}</td></tr>
    <tr><td>cover size  |U|</td><td>${s.U}</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Σ₁ = ∑|Aₐ|</td><td>${s.S1}</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Σ₂ = ∑<sub>i≠j</sub>|Aₐ∩A⫺|</td><td>${s.S2}</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Σ₂<sup>tot</sup> (with diagonal)</td><td>${s.S2t}</td></tr>
    <tr><td>double collisions |D|</td><td>${s.D}</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Bonferroni defect ∑(d−1)²</td><td>${s.defect}</td></tr>
    <tr><td>sharp defect ∑(d−1)(d−2)</td><td>${s.sharp}</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Cauchy–Schwarz gap g</td><td>${s.gap}</td></tr>
    <tr><td>multiplicity spread</td><td>${s.mx - s.mn}</td></tr>
    <tr><td>certificate spread ≤ √g</td><td>${
      (s.mx-s.mn)*(s.mx-s.mn) <= s.gap
        ? '<span class="chip ok">holds</span>' : '<span class="chip no">FAILS</span>'}</td></tr>
  `;

  // identities
  const maxTot = Math.max(s.S1+s.defect, 2*s.S1+s.sharp, 1);
  document.getElementById('ident1').innerHTML =
    stackRow('Σ₁ + defect',
      [{v:s.S1,c:'#5aa9e6',t:'Σ₁'},{v:s.defect,c:'#ff8080',t:'defect'}],
      s.S1+s.defect, maxTot) +
    stackRow('|U| + Σ₂',
      [{v:s.U,c:'#6ddf9f',t:'|U|'},{v:s.S2,c:'#ffc76b',t:'Σ₂'}],
      s.U+s.S2, maxTot);
  document.getElementById('ident2').innerHTML =
    stackRow('2Σ₁ + sharp defect',
      [{v:2*s.S1,c:'#5aa9e6',t:'2Σ₁'},{v:s.sharp,c:'#ff8080',t:'sharp'}],
      2*s.S1+s.sharp, maxTot) +
    stackRow('2|U| + Σ₂',
      [{v:2*s.U,c:'#6ddf9f',t:'2|U|'},{v:s.S2,c:'#ffc76b',t:'Σ₂'}],
      2*s.U+s.S2, maxTot);

  // verdict
  const disjoint = s.covered.every(v=>v===1);
  const le2 = s.covered.every(v=>v<=2);
  const regular = s.mx===s.mn;
  const chip = (b,txt)=>`<span class="chip ${b?'ok':'no'}">${txt}</span>`;
  let advice;
  if(disjoint) advice = 'Pairwise disjoint: the union bound itself is lossless, and so is every refinement of it.';
  else if(regular && le2) advice = 'A 2-regular cover: both the sharp Bonferroni bound and the Cauchy–Schwarz bound are exactly tight.';
  else if(regular) advice = 'A regular cover: the Cauchy–Schwarz / Corrádi bound is exactly tight, while Bonferroni is slack.';
  else if(le2) advice = 'Multiplicity at most two: the sharp Bonferroni bound and the double-collision bound are exactly tight.';
  else advice = 'Some point is covered three or more times and the coverage is uneven: no second-order bound is tight here — only the exact defect identities describe the family.';
  document.getElementById('verdict').innerHTML = `
    <div class="eq">${chip(disjoint,'pairwise disjoint')}
      ${chip(le2,'multiplicity ≤ 2')}${chip(regular,'regular cover')}</div>
    <div class="eq">Bonferroni slack <b>${(s.U+s.S2)-s.S1}</b>  · 
      sharp slack <b>${(2*s.U+s.S2)-2*s.S1}</b>  · 
      double-collision slack <b>${s.S2-2*s.D}</b></div>
    <div class="verdict">${advice}</div>`;

  // corradi
  const denom = s.m + (ROWS-1)*s.t;
  const lb = denom>0 ? (ROWS*s.m*s.m)/denom : 0;
  const tight = Math.abs(lb - s.U) < 1e-9;
  document.getElementById('corradi').innerHTML = `
    <tr><td>min first marginal  m</td><td>${s.m}</td></tr>
    <tr><td>max pairwise overlap  t</td><td>${s.t}</td></tr>
    <tr><td>envelope  k m²/(m+(k−1)t)</td><td>${lb.toFixed(4)}</td></tr>
    <tr><td>measured |U|</td><td>${s.U}</td></tr>
    <tr><td>status</td><td>${tight
      ? '<span class="chip ok">Corrádi tight</span>'
      : '<span class="chip no">strict</span>'}</td></tr>`;
}

preset('triangle');
</script>
</body>
</html>

<script>
function popcount(x){ let c=0; while(x){ c += x&1; x>>=1; } return c; }

function build(k){
  // families as arrays of Sets of integers 2*mask + bit
  const plain=[], parity=[];
  for(let i=0;i<k;i++){ plain.push(new Set()); parity.push(new Set()); }
  for(let mask=0; mask<(1<<k); mask++){
    const size = popcount(mask);
    const rightParity = ((size + k) % 2) === 0;
    for(let i=0;i<k;i++){
      if((mask>>i)&1){
        plain[i].add(2*mask);
        if(rightParity){ parity[i].add(2*mask); parity[i].add(2*mask+1); }
      }
    }
  }
  return {plain, parity};
}

function inter(fam, idx){
  let out = new Set(fam[idx[0]]);
  for(let a=1;a<idx.length;a++){
    const nxt = new Set();
    for(const v of out) if(fam[idx[a]].has(v)) nxt.add(v);
    out = nxt;
  }
  return out.size;
}

function cover(fam){
  const out = new Set();
  fam.forEach(s=>s.forEach(v=>out.add(v)));
  return out.size;
}

function combos(n, r){
  const res=[], cur=[];
  (function rec(start){
    if(cur.length===r){ res.push(cur.slice()); return; }
    for(let i=start;i<n;i++){ cur.push(i); rec(i+1); cur.pop(); }
  })(0);
  return res;
}

### A guided tour of coverage multiplicity, exact Bonferroni defects, and the marginal-order wall

---

## 0. The question, in one picture

You have $k$ sets. You know how big each one is. You know how big every pairwise
intersection is. **How big is the union?**

That is the whole subject. It sounds like an exercise, and its first answer —
inclusion–exclusion — is an exercise. But inclusion–exclusion needs data of
*every* order: all $2^k - 1$ intersections. In practice you only ever measure
the first two orders. So the real question is:

> How much does first- and second-order data determine, and how much does it
> provably fail to determine?

By the end of this page you will know the complete answer. Both halves of it are
sharp, and both come from a single scalar function.

<details>
<summary><b>New to this? Click for the one-paragraph orientation.</b></summary>

If the sets are pairwise disjoint, the union is exactly the sum of the sizes. If
they all coincide, the union is one of them. Everything in between is controlled
by *how many sets each point belongs to*. That number — the coverage
multiplicity — is the hero of this page. Read the
[inclusion–exclusion principle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inclusion%E2%80%93exclusion_principle)
and the [Boole–Bonferroni inequalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boole%27s_inequality)
if you want the classical background first; nothing below assumes it.

</details>

---

## 1. One function to rule them all

Fix a finite ground set $\Omega$ and a family $A_1, \dots, A_k \subseteq \Omega$.
Define the **coverage multiplicity**

$$d(x) \;=\; \#\{\, i : x \in A_i \,\},$$

and let $U = \bigcup_i A_i$ be the **cover**, i.e. $\{x : d(x) \ge 1\}$.

Two counting arguments — each one just Fubini for an incidence relation — give
everything:

$$\sum_{x \in U} d(x) \;=\; \sum_i |A_i|, \qquad\qquad
\sum_{x \in U} d(x)^2 \;=\; \sum_{i,j} |A_i \cap A_j|.$$

Read that again, because it is the crux. **The first- and second-order marginals
of a family are exactly the first two moments of one scalar function on the
cover.** Everything provable from pairwise data is a statement about
$(\mathbb{E}\,d, \mathbb{E}\,d^2)$; everything those two moments cannot see, the
pairwise data cannot see either.

Peeling off the diagonal gives the form we will use constantly:

$$\Sigma_2 \;:=\; \sum_{i \neq j}|A_i \cap A_j| \;=\; \sum_{x \in U} d(x)\bigl(d(x) - 1\bigr).$$

**Play with it now.** In the sandbox below, click cells to build any family you
like on a small ground set. The bottom row of the incidence matrix is $d(x)$;
every number in the dossier on the right is computed from that row alone.

## 2. The inequalities are identities in disguise

Here is the move that organises the entire theory. Take a pointwise polynomial
inequality for the integer $d$, sum it over the cover, and substitute the two
moment identities. Because the pointwise inequality comes from *dropping a
nonnegative term*, what you actually get is an **identity**, and the inequality
is its shadow.

### The Bonferroni defect identity

From $2d = 1 + d^2 - (d-1)^2$:

$$\sum_i |A_i| \;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{x \in U} \bigl(d(x)-1\bigr)^2}_{\text{irregularity}} \;=\; |U| \;+\; \sum_{i \neq j}|A_i \cap A_j|.$$

Drop the middle term and you have the classical second Bonferroni inequality.
Keep it and you know *exactly* what the inequality costs: the total squared
deviation of the multiplicity from $1$.

### The sharp version

The classical statement sums over unordered pairs and is a factor two stronger.
Its defect has a different, more revealing shape:

$$2\sum_i |A_i| \;+\; \sum_{x \in U}\bigl(d(x)-1\bigr)\bigl(d(x)-2\bigr) \;=\; 2|U| \;+\; \sum_{i \neq j}|A_i \cap A_j|.$$

The defect $(d-1)(d-2)$ vanishes on the whole interval $\{1,2\}$, not just at
$1$. That single change is why the sharp bound has a wider extremal class.

**In the sandbox above**, the "two exact defect identities" panel draws each side
of both identities as a stacked bar. They are always the same length. Try
loading *Mixed quad* and watching the red defect segment grow as you add
overlaps.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the derivation of the Bonferroni defect identity.</b></summary>

By the off-diagonal identity and the first-moment identity, the right-hand side is

$$|U| + \sum_{x\in U} d(x)(d(x)-1) = \sum_{x \in U}\Bigl(1 + d(x)^2 - d(x)\Bigr),$$

while the left-hand side is $\sum_{x \in U}\bigl(d(x) + (d(x)-1)^2\bigr) = \sum_{x\in U}\bigl(d(x) + d(x)^2 - 2d(x) + 1\bigr)$.
The two summands are the same polynomial. The only subtlety is over the natural
numbers, where one first writes $d(x) = 1 + c$ with $c \ge 0$ — legitimate
precisely because $d \ge 1$ on the cover — so that the subtraction is genuine
rather than truncated.

</details>

---

## 3. Rigidity: exactly who is extremal

Because each inequality is an identity minus a *sum of nonnegative terms*, it is
an equality exactly when every term vanishes. That converts three analytic
questions into three combinatorial ones, and each has a clean answer:

| bound | tight if and only if |
|---|---|
| second Bonferroni $\;\Sigma_1 \le \lvert U\rvert + \Sigma_2$ | the family is **pairwise disjoint** ($d \equiv 1$) |
| sharp Bonferroni & double collision $\;2\lvert D\rvert \le \Sigma_2$ | **no point is covered three times** ($d \le 2$) |
| Cauchy–Schwarz $\;\Sigma_1^2 \le \lvert U\rvert \cdot \Sigma_2^{\mathrm{tot}}$ | the cover is **regular** ($d$ constant) |

Here $D = \{x : d(x) \ge 2\}$ is the set of points where two members collide.
The last line needs one extra ingredient, the
[Lagrange identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagrange%27s_identity)
$2\bigl(|S|\sum f^2 - (\sum f)^2\bigr) = \sum_{x,y}(f(x)-f(y))^2$ — apply it with
$f = d$ and the gap becomes a manifest sum of squared multiplicity differences.

The classifier below turns those characterisations into an algorithm. Notice its
complexity claim: it never forms a single pairwise intersection, because the
factorial-moment identity lets it read $\Sigma_2$ straight off the multiplicity
map in linear time.
